proposed_widenings.name: FeatRecord + FeatMechanics family
proposed_widenings.justification: UnitRecord = SpellRecord | ClassFeatureRecord | MasteryRecord. There is no 'feat' kind. The v4 taxonomy has feat_root as a source atom, but the surface has no FeatRecord type and no FeatMechanics family. Magic Initiate cannot be placed into any existing record shape without lying about what it is.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Magic Initiate is an Origin Feat. UnitRecord has no feat variant.

proposed_widenings.name: grant_spell_access effect
proposed_widenings.justification: The core mechanic grants cantrips and a prepared level-1 spell from a chosen class spell list. ClassFeatureEffect only supports grant_extra_action and heal_hp. Even if FeatRecord existed, this effect type is absent from the surface. grant_spell_access exists in the v4 atom taxonomy but is not in ClassFeatureEffect nor in any typed effect union.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You learn two cantrips of your choice from the Cleric, Druid, or Wizard spell list... Choose a level 1 spell from the same list... You always have that spell prepared.

proposed_widenings.name: free_cast_once_per_rest resource pattern
proposed_widenings.justification: The Level 1 Spell benefit permits one free cast per Long Rest AND normal slot-based casting of the same spell. UseCountResource models a consumable pool; it does not model 'one free cast path plus an unlimited spell-slot path for the same spell.' A new resource variant is needed for this dual-access pattern.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You can cast it once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast the spell using any spell slots you have.

proposed_widenings.name: spellcasting_ability_choice (build-time choice binding)
proposed_widenings.justification: The feat requires choosing Int, Wis, or Cha as the spellcasting ability at feat acquisition. No surface type encodes a build-time ability choice that binds to the feat's granted spells.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this feat's spells (choose when you select this feat).

notes: Primary blocker is structural: no FeatRecord in UnitRecord. The remaining three widenings are surface_widening concerns within the feat family and cannot be resolved until the structural gap is closed. Spell Change (swap a spell on level-up) and Repeatable (take feat multiple times with different lists) are character-progression metadata with no deterministic combat-mechanic consequence; they would be authoring annotations rather than typed mechanics and are not counted as widenings.
